classification.difficultyReason: Read a marked function value and reflect a supplied curve, its point and asymptote on shared axes.

spec.description: Increasing concave-up curve through the origin and marked point (1,1), with dashed coordinate guides and horizontal asymptote y=-1. Axes and labels reproduce the supplied graph.
spec.mathematics: The source supplies a qualitative graph without an equation. Bézier segments reconstruct its visible shape and exact supplied points; no analytic function rule is inferred.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent supplied graph; the numerical value f(1) is left for the student.

answer.short:
$f(1)=1$.

Reflect the supplied curve in $y=x$. Its inverse passes through $(0,0)$ and $(1,1)$ and has vertical asymptote $x=-1$. Include $y=x$ on the same axes.
answer.worked:
The marked point $(1,1)$ gives $f(1)=1$. Reflect each point $(a,b)$ on $y=f(x)$ to $(b,a)$ on $y=f^{-1}(x)$.

The points $(0,0)$ and $(1,1)$ remain fixed. The horizontal asymptote $y=-1$ reflects to the vertical asymptote $x=-1$. Draw both curves and $y=x$ on one Cartesian plane.

spec.description: Original curve in blue, its exact coordinate-swapped reflection in red, dashed line y=x, reflected asymptotes and marked point (1,1).
spec.mathematics: Each Bézier endpoint and control point in the supplied-curve reconstruction is swapped to construct the inverse. The source specifies y=-1, giving inverse asymptote x=-1; no equation is invented.
